about: Research sheet for the Wyoming county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Wyoming
phones_sentence: Wyoming’s veterans service officers are reached through the Veterans Commission’s statewide line, 1-800-833-5987, which connects you to the officer who covers your county.

offices.note: Veterans service officers help with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and state veterans benefits at no charge.
offices.selection: Wyoming has no county veterans offices. The Veterans Commission’s site (read in full) gives its Cheyenne office and main number but no list of service officers by county, and the Department of Health says to call the Veterans Hotline, 1-800-833-5987, to meet with one (https://health.wyo.gov/aging/veteranshome/veterans-resources/; search excerpt). Every county shows that statewide line. County-by-county coverage maps found online date from 2020 and are not official, so they are not used.

aging.source_title: Wyoming Department of Health, Aging Division: Services by county (service area maps)
aging.source_scope: Every provider by county, with its town, phone and services (supportive services, meals, caregiver support, Wyoming Home Services); read in full; page updated October 20, 2026. Each county card leads with the senior center in the county seat (Big Horn County: the center offering the most programs) and lists the county’s other providers. Foster Grandparent and Senior Companion volunteer programs are left out. The page lists Goshen County’s providers under Crook County, so Crook County shows the Aging Division’s statewide line (https://health.wyo.gov/aging: 307-777-7995, 800-442-2766; search excerpt).
aging.description: Senior centers in each county, funded by the Wyoming Department of Health’s Aging Division, provide supportive services, meals, caregiver support and Wyoming Home Services for older adults. You apply for services directly through the senior center.
aging.next_step_extra: The state Aging Division can also help, 1-800-442-2766, and Wyoming 2-1-1 lists more local services.

programs.name: Wyoming veterans: Veterans Commission service officers for claims help
programs.description: Free help with VA disability and pension claims, health care and state and federal benefits from the Wyoming Veterans Commission’s veterans service officers. Call the statewide line to meet with the officer who covers your area.
programs.next_step: Call the Wyoming Veterans Hotline, 1-800-833-5987, and ask to meet with a veterans service officer.
constraints: Service officers travel to outreach sites; call ahead to set a time.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (Wyoming State Health Insurance Information Program)
programs.organization: Wyoming Senior Citizens, Inc., Wyoming State Health Insurance Information Program (WSHIIP)
programs.description: Free, one-on-one Medicare counseling from Wyoming’s State Health Insurance Information Program, Wyoming’s SHIP: Medicare, Medicare Savings Programs, prescription drug help and supplemental insurance.
programs.next_step: Call WSHIIP toll-free at 1-800-856-4398. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Counseling is by appointment. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

programs.name: Wyoming Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Wyoming Department of Health, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program; Department of Family Services, Adult Protective Services
programs.description: Advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and other long-term care settings, through three regional ombudsman offices. Adult Protective Services, in the Department of Family Services, takes reports of abuse, neglect or exploitation of vulnerable adults.
programs.next_step: Choose a county above for its regional ombudsman, or call 1-800-856-4398. To report abuse, call your local Department of Family Services office (an on-call caseworker is available 24 hours a day), Adult Protective Services at 307-777-3602, or local law enforcement. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for older Wyoming residents
programs.description: Legal Aid of Wyoming is funded by the Aging Division to provide supportive services for older adults, with offices in Cheyenne, Casper, Gillette and Lander.
programs.next_step: Call the nearest Legal Aid of Wyoming office: Cheyenne 307-432-0808, Casper 307-232-9830, Gillette 307-459-5765, Lander 307-332-3517.
constraints: Legal aid screens by age, income and case type.

programs.name: VA health care in Wyoming
programs.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs: VA Cheyenne and VA Sheridan health care systems
programs.description: Wyoming veterans are served by two VA health care systems: the Cheyenne VA Medical Center (2360 E. Pershing Blvd.; 307-778-7550, toll-free 888-483-9127) and the Sheridan VA Medical Center (1898 Fort Road; 307-672-3473), each with community clinics.
programs.next_step: Call Cheyenne at 307-778-7550 or Sheridan at 307-672-3473 for appointments or VA Health Connect. Not enrolled yet? Ask a veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.
